author: BeauHD
description: The open-source Ladybird web browser has reached its alpha milestone after four years of development, offering an independent browser engine built from scratch rather than forked from Chromium, Firefox or another existing engine. Alpha builds are now available for macOS and Linux, including Flatpak packages and binaries for Ubuntu and Fedora. Phoronix reports: As for the expected alpha state: "Ladybird is a browser with a new engine. The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork. The browser around it is modest, but functional. This is an alpha, so some websites won't work, and it will crash sometimes. When that happens, tell us! You can report a broken site from inside the browser."
title: Ladybird Web Browser/Engine Reaches Alpha

author: BeauHD
description: The U.S. Commerce Department plans to blacklist Singapore-based AI infrastructure company Megaspeed and its subsidiary Speedmatrix over suspicions that they helped Chinese companies obtain restricted Nvidia AI chips. The move follows allegations that a former Megaspeed executive had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang while working as a Chinese intelligence asset, although Commerce officials say their investigation into the company began nearly two years ago. The BBC reports: The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US. The company is mainly a developer of data centers, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang. [...] When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency
title: US To Blacklist Asian AI Firm Megaspeed After Nvidia Scandal

author: BeauHD
description:
Western intelligence agencies reportedly believe Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit as early as December, "suggesting the country's development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought," reports Ars Technica, citing German media reports. Such a launch would violate the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, while a detonation could create radiation belts that damage satellites for years. From the report: The orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia's own spacecraft and Chinese satellites.
 
Reporting from three German news outlets -- public broadcasters NDR and WDR
title: Russia May Launch Nuclear Weapon Into Orbit As Soon As Next Month

author: BeauHD
description: An anonymous reader quotes a report from WGNA-FM: On November 23rd, New York State Governor Kathy Hochul announced Bill S.9348A/A.10411A. This bill aims to put money back in New Yorkers pockets by prohibiting any vehicle manufacturers, dealers, or third-party providers from charging consumers more money for locked services or subscription fees. This specifically targets newer vehicles that may lock pre-installed features (like heated seats or screen compatibility) behind a paywall or subscription service. This is becoming more and more of a problem as years go by, and consumers have been very vocal against the practice, but this is a tangible step that can be taken to end this practice before it gets too out of hand. [...] The bill will go into effect on February 27th, 2027. "No one should have to pay recurring fees just to use features in a car they already bought. My office has secured millions of dollars for New Yorkers throughout the state who were charged illegal junk fees when p
title: New York Bans Subscription and Post-Purchase Fees On Cars

author: BeauHD
description: Google is shutting down its 15-year-old Nest app on January 25, 2027, requiring users to switch to Google Home to remotely control their smart home devices and receive notifications. "Then, on August 2, the company will retire Google Assistant on smart speakers and displays, with Gemini replacing the older tech for voice controls," reports Engadget. From the report: If you've yet to migrate your Nest devices to the Google Home app, the company says your existing settings and schedules will transfer over automatically. The only thing you need to manually move over are any custom clips you might have saved over the years. You can do this by visiting the Nest website before January 25 and clicking the "Download all" button. Google says it will automatically migrate Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions to its newer Google Home Premium package. title: Google Is Finally Retiring the Nest App Early Next Year
